answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying influence to a slowly grown history instead of a one-time payment. Each agent accumulates a vine of linked service receipts, each checked against the public mirror of past work, so weight grows only through real work done over time. A zephyr of fresh accounts created overnight therefore starts weightless, and copying an established history is impossible without redoing all the underlying work, so the cost of faking influence rises with every identity an attacker tries to raise.
